findings.plain_summary: OPM is seeking public comment, through December 18, 2026, on a new one-time application form that tribal employers (tribes, tribal organizations, tribally controlled schools, and urban Indian organizations) would complete to participate in the FEHB Program under 25 U.S.C. 1647b and 5 CFR part 890 subpart N. The form collects identifying information, key personnel, billing unit and bank account details, and an employer profile; OPM estimates 75 respondents at 2.25 hours each, for 168.75 total burden hours.

items.headline: New one-time application collects tribal employers' bank account and billing information
items.what_changes: Tribal employers applying to FEHB would submit identifying information, representatives, key personnel, billing unit and bank account information, and an employer profile. The summary does not describe the form's contents.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: This collection consists of information identifying the tribal employer and its representatives for FEHB purposes, key tribal personnel, billing unit and bank account information, and a tribal employer profile. Collection of this information is necessary to ensure the validity of a program application and to facilitate enrollment in the FEHB Program.

items.headline: Burden estimate: 75 tribal employers, 2.25 hours each, 168.75 total hours
items.what_changes: OPM estimates 75 respondents completing the application once, at 135 minutes each.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote:
Number of Respondents: 75.
    Estimated Time per Respondent: 135 minutes or 2.25 hours.
    Total Burden Hours: 168.75.

items.headline: Comment deadline is December 18, 2026
items.what_changes: This is a 60-day comment period, and comments are accepted at regulations.gov. Submissions are posted publicly without change, including personal identifiers.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Comments are encouraged and will be accepted until December 18, 2026.

items.headline: Once the employer elects in, eligible tribal employees can enroll in FEHB
items.what_changes: The application is the gateway for tribal employers' participation. After an employer elects to participate under 5 CFR 890.1404, its common-law employees who meet FEHB employment-type requirements become eligible to enroll under 890.1405.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Once a tribal employer elects to participate in the FEHB Program in compliance with 5 CFR 890.1404, a tribal employee who is considered a common law employee and meets FEHB requirements for the type of employment (e.g., full-time, seasonal) will become eligible to enroll in FEHB pursuant to 5 CFR 890.1405.

items.headline: Which employers qualify as "tribal employers"
items.what_changes: The covered employers are tribes or tribal organizations running at least one program under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act or the Tribally Controlled Schools Act. Urban Indian organizations running at least one program under title V of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act also qualify.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM defines ``tribal employer'' in 5 CFR 890.1402 to include an Indian tribe or tribal organization carrying out at least one program under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act or the Tribally Controlled Schools Act; or an urban Indian organization carrying out at least one program under title V of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act.

could_not_determine: How many tribal employees would become eligible for or enroll in FEHB as a result of tribal employer participation.
Whether the 75-respondent estimate reflects all eligible tribal employers or only those expected to apply.
Whether this form replaces an existing application process or OMB-approved collection for tribal employers.
Any dollar cost estimate for respondents (only hours are given).
Whether the application will be submitted electronically or on paper, and how OPM will protect the bank account information.
The actual content of the form, which is not reproduced in the notice.
